brief: Goldman's Prime Brokerage data shows hedge funds net sold US stocks for a second straight week despite the S&P rising 2.5% and semis rallying over 8%, their best week since April, as the AI trade absorbed Nvidia's CEO departure, a third hot CPI and a Fed governor floating a 50bp hike. Unlike the prior week's long liquidation, this week's selling came mostly from fresh single-stock shorts: funds covered index and ETF hedges (shorts fell 8.6%) while adding new shorts in individual names, led by Info Tech (long/short ratio at a record low 1.5), Financials (99th percentile selling) and Health Care, even though both Financials and Health Care remain crowded overweights funds had used to hide from the AI unwind. Leverage ticked up, but from the market's rise and index-hedge covering rather than buying, and net exposure stays near five-year lows. October was multi-PM funds' worst month on record, worse than March 2020, in a year the S&P is up double digits. Bulls (Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Goldman's macro desk) say the light positioning sets up a year-end squeeze; Goldman's own strategist calls it a low-consensus 'blank slate,' while heavy VIX-put buying signals skepticism the rally itself extends.
